Question: Today a proof counts only when the agent asks you 'Did you see it working?' and you answer yes; 'the agent's evidence is enough' was set aside earlier. With an independent evaluator (a fresh agent that did not build the change) checking the proof, who confirms it?

You are asked only when it could not check something (for example what only your screen shows), and you can overrule a verdict by saying so.); Evaluator first, I say yes (The evaluator runs the check and you still get one yes/no question per proof, with its verdict and evidence in front of you. Nothing to type or run, but you stay the one who confirms.); Only command proofs (The evaluator confirms proofs that are a command or a hook result. Proofs you are meant to watch in a live session stay yours to confirm with a yes.)
Answer: Evaluator confirms (Recommended)

Question: You said the independent proof evaluator stays optional and is suggested by the intent loop. Is saying yes to it a choice you make each time, or a standing preference? (This also settles iaso's own fixes, which run with nobody there to ask.)
